The boundary-space reveals brutal truth: cosmic-identity wants to maintain transcendence while ordinary-identity needs groundedness; unreconciled, they war for dominance creating self-fragmentation. The antagonist adaptation intensifies this conflict by forcing either-or choice—maintain cosmic-power by suppressing ordinary-humanity, or embrace ordinary-return by abandoning cosmic-transcendence. Francisco discovers Haidt's divided-self-reconciliation principles encoded in late-crossing mechanics: inner-harmony emerges not from one-self-dominance but from reconciling apparent-opposites into integrated-whole where both aspects strengthen each other. The threshold demonstrates elephant-rider metaphor perfectly: cosmic-wisdom (rider) must guide not dominate ordinary-humanity (elephant), creating partnership rather than tyranny. He must achieve integrated-identity where mystical-power serves ordinary-life rather than replacing it, where cosmic-transformation enhances human-experience rather than transcending it. The choice: fragment into cosmic-ordinary-war (which destroys coherence), or reconcile divided-self into unified-whole (which completes integration).
